refuted_findings.issue: The Rule, Loop, score formula, clone taxonomy, and commit gates are already written out in full in this same SKILL.md body (The One Rule callout, The Loop, Opportunity Matrix, Duplication Taxonomy, Checklist). QUICK-REFERENCE.md isn't caching an expensive external lookup — the source is the very document the pointer sits in — so it's a second authoritative copy of the same meanings rather than a justified cache.
refuted_findings.proposed_fix: Point readers to the relevant sections of this file instead of a separately-maintained card, or make QUICK-REFERENCE.md the single source and replace these inline sections with pointers to it.
refuted_findings.reason: panel 0/3 confirmed | REFUTED — the quoted text does appear verbatim, but the "single source of truth" duplication rule from this refactoring skill applies to code, not to an intentionally-designed documentation quick-reference card; the skill explicitly frames QUICK-REFERENCE.md as a "return here for depth" summary layer, which is standard TL;DR documentation practice, not an unjustified duplicate authority. || REFUTED — the quote is verbatim but the "issue" mischaracterizes a normal quick-reference summary card as a duplication violation; summarizing detailed sections into a condensed one-screen card is standard documentation practice, not the kind of duplicate-source-of-truth problem the cited rule is meant to catch. || REFUTED — quoted text appears verbatim, but a condensed quick-reference card summarizing content already detailed in the same doc is a legitimate, common documentation pattern (not a "single source of truth" violation) since the two serve different purposes (depth vs. quick lookup) rather than being redundant authoritative copies.

refuted_findings.rule: Cut identity the body already states (Context pointers)
refuted_findings.target_quote:
Find where a codebase reinvents its own design system — raw colour literals,
one-off Tailwind arbitrary values, palette utilities, unresolved tokens, and
clusters that reveal a scale nobody defined
refuted_findings.issue: The description restates, in near-identical wording, the identity claim the body already makes for itself in its opening line: 'A detection skill. It does ONE thing: find where a codebase has drifted away from a design system — or never had one.' The pointer's job is to state when to reach the document, not to re-describe what it fundamentally is once the reader is already in it.
refuted_findings.proposed_fix: Trim the description to the branch-triggering clauses ('audit design consistency, derive a type or spacing scale, author a DESIGN.md from a messy codebase, or turn drift findings into a token architecture') and drop the restatement of 'find where a codebase reinvents/drifted from a design system,' since the body's opening paragraph already carries that identity statement.
refuted_findings.reason: panel 0/3 confirmed | REFUTED — the description is YAML frontmatter (metadata used for skill discovery/invocation before the body is ever read), not a redundant in-body pointer, so trimming it wouldn't serve the stated "cut identity the body already states" rationale. || REFUTED — the description text is frontmatter metadata read before the body is ever reached (used for skill selection), so it isn't a redundant "pointer" restating an already-in-context identity claim; the quoted text appears verbatim but the rule's premise doesn't apply. || REFUTED — the description text is frontmatter metadata (used for skill discovery/routing before the body is ever read), so restating identity there is not redundant in the way claimed; the quoted text does appear verbatim, but the rule's rationale (reader "already in it") doesn't apply since the description is read separately from the body.
